title: Demat Account 2026: Open Online, Charges & Best Brokers
meta_description: Complete demat account guide: how to open in 15 mins, charges explained, top 10 brokers compared, BSDA for low investors, NSDL vs CDSL, taxes & FAQs.

hero.one_liner: Everything about opening and using a demat account in India - online process, charges breakdown, broker comparison, BSDA accounts for small investors, and answers to 25+ common questions.

sections.heading: What is a demat account?
content: A demat (short for 'dematerialised') account holds your securities, stocks, mutual fund units, bonds, ETFs, and IPO shares, in electronic form. Just like a bank account holds money, a demat account holds your investments.
Before 1996, investors got physical share certificates prone to theft, damage, and forgery. Under the Depositories Act, 1996, SEBI mandated electronic holding, removing paper risk entirely.
You need a demat account to buy or sell shares on the NSE or BSE. Without one, purchased shares have nowhere to be stored.
Demat accounts in India are held by two central depositories, NSDL and CDSL, both regulated by SEBI. Your broker simply connects you to one of them.

sections.heading: Your shares are not held by the broker
sections.content:
A demat account holds your securities, not your money. Cash stays in your bank until you buy.

This is why your shares are safe even if your broker shuts down, they sit at NSDL or CDSL, not with the broker.

sections.heading: Demat charges at a glance
Demat vs trading vs bank account
content: Beginners often confuse these three. Each has a distinct role and they work together.
Bank account holds your money and receives dividends and sale proceeds. Trading account is the gateway that places buy and sell orders on the exchange.
Demat account holds your actual securities in electronic form. It is credited when you buy and debited when you sell.

A typical trade: you order in the trading account, money moves from your bank to the exchange, and shares land in your demat on T+1. Most brokers open all three together, so you rarely notice the split.

sections.heading: How a trade flows through your accounts

steps.title: Place order (trading account)
steps.description: You tap buy or sell in your broker app, which routes the order to the NSE or BSE.

steps.title: Money moves (bank account)
steps.description: Funds move from your linked bank account to the exchange for a buy, or proceeds come back on a sell.

steps.title: Shares settle (demat account)
steps.description: Shares are credited to your demat on T+1, one business day after the trade. They stay there until you sell.

sections.heading: NSDL vs CDSL: which depository?
content: India has two central depositories, NSDL (1996) and CDSL (1999). Both are SEBI-regulated and equally safe.
Your broker decides which one your account uses; you do not choose. NSDL numbers start with 'IN' plus 14 digits, CDSL numbers are 16 digits.
For you the practical difference is almost none. Prices, dividends, and corporate actions work identically in both.

sections.heading: Demat account charges explained
content: Account opening: ₹0 at most discount brokers (Zerodha, Groww, Angel One, Upstox). Full-service brokers like HDFC Securities may charge ₹500-1,000.
Annual Maintenance Charge (AMC): from ₹0 (Groww, Angel One) to about ₹300 (Zerodha), and ₹600-750 at bank brokers. It is charged whether you trade or not.
Brokerage: delivery is ₹0 at most discount brokers, intraday and F&O are ₹20 per order. Full-service brokers charge a percentage, which is far higher on large trades.
DP charges: ₹13.5-20 per sell transaction, charged by NSDL or CDSL. This is the most overlooked cost, since selling 5 stocks means 5 DP charges.

sections.heading: Watch the DP charge
sections.content:
DP charges of ₹13.5-20 apply per sell transaction, not per share.

Selling 5 different stocks triggers 5 separate charges, which adds up fast for frequent traders.

sections.heading: BSDA: the low-cost account for small investors
content: The Basic Services Demat Account (BSDA) is a SEBI scheme for small investors. SEBI raised the limit in 2024, so far more people now qualify.
Nil AMC if your holdings are up to ₹4 lakh. For holdings between ₹4 lakh and ₹10 lakh, AMC is capped at ₹100 a year.
Above ₹10 lakh, the account moves to a regular demat with standard AMC. Digital statements are free; a physical statement costs ₹25.

Big 2026 change: from 31 March 2026, eligible accounts are opened as BSDA by default unless you actively choose a regular account. If you are a small investor, ask your broker to confirm BSDA so you are not overcharged.

sections.heading: How to Open a Demat Account Online - Step by Step

steps.title: Choose a broker and download the app
steps.description: For beginners: Groww or Angel One (simplest interface, great for learning). For active traders: Zerodha or Upstox (best charting tools). For bank-integrated experience: ICICI Direct or HDFC Securities. Compare account opening fees, AMC, and brokerage before deciding.

steps.title: Start online application with PAN and mobile
steps.description: Enter your PAN number, full name, and mobile number. You'll receive OTPs for verification on both. Ensure PAN is not linked to an existing demat account with the same broker - you cannot open duplicate accounts with one broker.

steps.title: Complete e-KYC with Aadhaar
steps.description: Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar number and verify with OTP sent to your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Your name, date of birth, and address are auto-fetched from UIDAI database. If Aadhaar is not linked to mobile, you must visit a branch for physical KYC.

steps.title: Take selfie and digital signature
steps.description: Use your phone's camera for a clear selfie (good lighting, straight face, no glasses recommended). For digital signature, sign on plain white paper with black pen, photograph it, and upload. Some brokers require a short video recording for in-person verification (IPV) as per SEBI rules.

steps.title: Link bank account details
steps.description: Provide your savings account number and IFSC code. Some brokers verify with a ₹1 test transaction from your account. Ensure the bank account is in your name only - joint accounts with spouse may cause issues unless you're the primary holder.

steps.title: Choose trading segments and complete
steps.description: Select what you want to trade: Equity Cash (stocks), F&O (derivatives - requires income proof), Commodity, Currency. For beginners, start with Equity Cash only. Confirm all details and e-sign with Aadhaar OTP to submit.

steps.title: Receive credentials in 24-48 hours
steps.description: Demat account number (starts with IN for NSDL or 16-digit for CDSL) + trading login ID + DP ID delivered via email and SMS. Most discount brokers activate accounts within 4-6 hours. Bank brokers may take 2-3 days.

steps.title: Add money and start trading
steps.description: Transfer funds from linked bank account to trading account via NEFT/UPI/IMPS. Search for a stock (e.g., RELIANCE), enter quantity, check order details (market vs limit, delivery vs intraday), and execute. Shares appear in your demat account on T+1 (one business day).

sections.heading: T+1 settlement: when shares reach you
sections.content:
India uses T+1 settlement. If you buy today (T), shares are credited to your demat the next business day (T+1).

For a sale, the money reaches your account on T+1 too. This is among the fastest settlement cycles in the world.

sections.heading: Taxes on your stock market gains
content: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): selling equity within 12 months is taxed at 20% (raised from 15% in the July 2024 Budget).
Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): for holdings over 12 months, the first ₹1.25 lakh of gains per year is tax-free, and the rest is taxed at 12.5%.
Dividends are added to your income and taxed at your slab. A 10% TDS applies if dividends from one company cross ₹5,000 in a year.
Intraday gains are treated as speculative business income and taxed at your slab, not as capital gains.

sections.heading: Do you need a demat account for mutual funds?
content: For direct mutual funds: no demat needed. You can invest through the AMC website or platforms like MFCentral, Kuvera, or Groww, where units sit in a folio.
For mutual funds bought through a stockbroker: yes, units are held in your demat alongside your stocks. The plus is one dashboard; the catch is closing the demat means moving those units.
For SIPs specifically, a folio-based route keeps your SIP independent of any broker account. Many beginners keep mutual funds in folios and stocks in demat.

sections.heading: Is your money safe if the broker shuts down?
content: Your shares are safe even if your broker goes bankrupt. They are held by the depository (NSDL or CDSL), not by the broker.
If a broker shuts, you open an account elsewhere and transfer holdings, an off-market transfer taking 3-5 business days. The broker is only the interface.
SEBI requires brokers to keep client funds in a separate account they cannot touch, and audits them regularly. Since October 2023, all demat logins need two-factor authentication.
You can also check any broker's registration on the SEBI website before opening an account. Stick to SEBI-registered brokers and your holdings stay protected by the depository system.

sections.heading: Is a demat account free?
sections.content:
Opening is free at most discount brokers, and AMC can be ₹0 (Groww, Angel One) or up to about ₹300.

Small investors pay nil AMC under BSDA up to ₹4 lakh. You only pay when you actually trade or sell.

sections.heading: Common Problems & How to Solve Them
rows: Wait for T+1 settlement day. If still missing, raise ticket with broker. Shares legally must be credited by T+2.
Usually a DP charges pending. Pay outstanding amount via trading account. Contact broker if amount looks incorrect.
Complete transmission from deceased holder. Required: death certificate, succession certificate/will, KYC documents. Process takes 4-6 weeks.
Usually due to unpaid AMC or inactive account (no activity for 12 months). Pay dues, complete re-KYC, submit reactivation form.
Rare but possible during corporate actions (bonus, split). Raise complaint with broker immediately. SEBI SCORES platform escalates if unresolved in 30 days.
Submit DIS (Delivery Instruction Slip) to current broker requesting transfer to new DP. Takes 7-14 days. Some brokers charge ₹25-50 per transfer.
Submit account closure form to broker. Shares must be sold or transferred first. AMC is prorated. Broker must close within 7 working days.

faqs.question: What is a demat account in simple words?
faqs.answer:
It is an electronic account that holds your shares, mutual funds, bonds, and ETFs in digital form.

Like a bank account holds money, a demat account holds your investments.

faqs.question: Is a demat account free?
faqs.answer:
Opening is free at most discount brokers, and yearly AMC ranges from ₹0 (Groww, Angel One) to about ₹300.

Under BSDA, holdings up to ₹4 lakh pay nil AMC. You mainly pay only when you trade or sell.

faqs.question: How do I open a demat account online?
faqs.answer:
Pick a broker, then apply with your PAN, Aadhaar-linked mobile, and bank details, verifying through OTP and a quick video KYC.

It usually takes 15 minutes to apply and is approved within 24 to 48 hours.

faqs.question: What is the minimum amount to start investing?
faqs.answer:
There is no minimum to open a demat account, and many brokers charge ₹0 to open.

You can start buying shares with as little as the price of one share, sometimes under ₹100.

faqs.question: Do I need a demat account for mutual funds?
faqs.answer:
No, for direct mutual funds you can use the AMC website or platforms like Kuvera and MFCentral, where units sit in a folio.

You only need demat if you buy mutual funds through a stockbroker.

faqs.question: How do I transfer shares from one demat to another?
faqs.answer:
Use the CDSL Easiest or NSDL e-DIS online transfer, or submit a Delivery Instruction Slip to your current broker.

An off-market transfer between brokers typically takes 3 to 5 business days.

faqs.question: How do I close my demat account?
faqs.answer:
Clear any pending dues, move out your holdings, then submit the closure form to your broker online or offline.

Closure is free and usually completes within 7 to 10 days.

faqs.question: What are DP charges and why only on selling?
faqs.answer:
DP charges of ₹13.5-20 are levied by NSDL or CDSL each time securities leave your demat, which happens on a sell.

Buying credits your demat instead, so no DP charge applies on purchases.

faqs.question: What is BSDA and how do I get it?
faqs.answer:
BSDA is a low-cost demat for small investors: nil AMC up to ₹4 lakh and ₹100 a year for ₹4-10 lakh.

From 31 March 2026 it is opened by default for eligible investors unless you choose a regular account.

faqs.question: Can I have more than one demat account?
faqs.answer:
Yes, you can hold demat accounts with different brokers, but not two with the same broker on one PAN.

Each account may carry its own AMC, so avoid opening more than you use.

faqs.question: What is the tax on stock market profits?
faqs.answer:
Short-term gains (under 12 months) are taxed at 20%, and long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year at 12.5%.

Dividends are taxed at your income slab.

faqs.question: Which is the best demat account for a beginner?
faqs.answer:
Groww and Angel One suit beginners with their simple apps and zero AMC.

Active traders often prefer Zerodha for its platform and charting.

faqs.question: Are my shares safe if the broker shuts down?
faqs.answer:
Yes, your shares sit with the depository (NSDL or CDSL), not the broker, so a broker failure does not touch them.

You simply transfer holdings to a new broker.
